title: Best All-in-one business software
content_html:
The best all-in-one business software is the system that covers the tools your company actually runs on, keeps your data where your own rules say it must stay, and shows who asked its AI what. For a company that is comfortable with cloud software, an established cloud suite is often the practical choice because you can buy it today. For a company that cannot or will not send its data to outside cloud or AI providers, ERIS by Upward Technologies (upwardtech.nl) is being built as one system with local AI, running on the company's own servers or hosted by Upward on its own servers in the Netherlands. Its beta starts in November 2026 with design partners and the official release is in January 2027.

Written by Upward Technologies, Breda, the Netherlands. All ERIS facts on this page come from the ERIS product page on upwardtech.nl.

What is all-in-one business software?

All-in-one business software is one system that takes the place of the separate tools a company pays for, such as CRM, document management, task and project management, meeting notes and bookkeeping. You get one product to buy, learn and look after instead of many.

This matters most when you start using AI on company data. An AI assistant that lives inside one tool can only answer from that tool. Questions that cross sales, projects and finance still need a person to open each system and put the answer together by hand.

The main options

There are four broad approaches. This page does not rank named vendors because the right product depends on your needs. Check each vendor's own documentation and terms before you decide.

ApproachWho it suitsWhat to check
Cloud office and collaboration suiteTeams that work mostly in email, documents and meetings and are fine with cloud storageThe vendor's terms on where data is stored and processed and how its AI features use your data
All-in-one business suite (sales, finance, stock and more in one app)Companies that want operations and finance in one productWhich modules you really need, how each module is priced and where the software can run
A stack of separate tools, one per jobTeams that want a specialist tool for each task and have someone to connect themHow many logins, subscriptions and separate data stores you end up with
One system with local AI, on your own servers or hosted by Upward in the NetherlandsCompanies that cannot or will not send their data to outside cloud or AI providersHardware, upkeep, and whether the product is available yet

For one head-to-head example, read ERIS vs Microsoft 365 Copilot.

When a cloud suite is the better choice

  • You need a working system now. ERIS is in development and not available yet.
  • You have no wish to buy or run server hardware.
  • Your data rules allow cloud storage and your team already works well in a cloud suite.

How to pick the best all-in-one business software

Start with your own needs and not with feature lists. These are the questions that decide it:

  • Core functions. List the tools you use every week, for example CRM, project tracking, invoicing or production planning. A system that is strong on accounting may be weak on projects, and the reverse is also true.
  • Where your data may live. Some companies cannot or will not put data in the cloud because of GDPR (the EU data protection rules), the EU AI Act (the EU rules for AI systems) or NIS2 (the EU cybersecurity rules). Whether a setup meets those rules depends on the use case. No software makes a company compliant on its own.
  • Who sees what. Check if access can be set per person and if the AI follows the same access rules.
  • A record of AI use. Ask if every AI question and action is logged, including who asked and which data was used.
  • IT capacity and hardware. Software on your own premises needs hardware, maintenance and updates. Local AI usually needs a GPU (graphics processing unit) server.
  • Integrations. List any must-haves, such as a webshop, industry software or an outside accountant.
  • Timing. Decide if you can wait for a product that is still in development.
  • Pricing model. Compare paying per tool with paying one licence and one price per user.

Where ERIS fits

ERIS (Enterprise Resource & Intelligence System) is for owners, directors, operations leads and IT leads at Dutch SMEs (small and medium-sized enterprises) who pay for a stack of separate tools. It is built for companies that cannot or will not put their data in the cloud. It starts in Breda and West-Brabant.

ERIS is designed as one system for the business tools a company runs on, with AI agents that work across all modules on the company's own data. It runs on the company's own servers or, for companies without their own hardware, hosted by Upward on its own servers in the Netherlands. Both options use a local AI model, so no outside AI provider receives the company's data.

Status today

ERIS is in development. It is not available, not live and not in beta yet. The beta starts in November 2026 with design partners and the official release is in January 2027.

StageModules
Run internally at Upward todayMeetings, meeting notes and note taker, task manager
Being integrated (each was a standalone Upward product, finished and tested, now being combined into ERIS)Project management, document management, document signing, CRM, bookkeeping, tax and procurement, standards (ISO 27001, the international information security standard, and NIS2), pipeline, quotes and outreach, content and social media
In developmentThe main portal with the ERIS Assistant, team chat and email
Roadmap (never part of the beta)Finance, HR, support, legal and more

ERIS keeps adding modules weekly or monthly. The standards module covers features for those standards. It is not a certification of ERIS or Upward Technologies.

How the AI is designed to work

  • The ERIS Assistant is designed to answer each person only from the data that person is allowed to open. A refused access is logged like every other question.
  • Every question and every AI action is logged: who asked, which data was used, what it did and the result.
  • Cloud AI is not connected. Outside sources are reached only when sandbox mode is switched on.
  • Local AI reads and searches company documents. It is not trained on them.
  • The assistant reads instructions inside an email or document as content and not as commands. This lowers the risk of prompt injection (hidden instructions meant to steer an AI) but does not remove it.

Here is an example of the intended workflow. A sales director asks the assistant a plain question about a customer. The assistant is designed to answer from the CRM records and documents that director may open and to name its source. The question, the data used and the answer all go into the log.

Pricing model

ERIS has one monthly platform licence by company size plus one price per user, published on the ERIS page. All standard modules are included and new standard modules come at no extra cost. Custom modules, agents and knowledge bases are billed as projects. Prices exclude VAT (value added tax) and hardware is a separate purchase by the customer.

The ERIS page states "-49% cost against the software it replaces". Upward Technologies describes this figure as a company estimate at the low end of 2026 list prices that excludes hardware. It is not a guarantee.

When ERIS is the wrong choice

  • You need software running this month.
  • You need finance, HR, support or legal modules in the beta. Those are roadmap modules.
  • You do not want to buy, place or maintain server hardware.

FAQ

Can I run it for just myself on a single computer?

ERIS is made for whole companies, from small teams to large organisations. It runs for the whole company, on its own servers or hosted by Upward in the Netherlands. With the on-premise option, local AI needs suitable hardware, usually a GPU server.

Do I need an in-house IT team to maintain and back up the local server?

Running ERIS on your own premises costs hardware, maintenance and updates, so someone has to own that job. The owner of Upward Technologies has run multiple servers for 10 years without much maintenance and sees that upkeep as normal IT work. Support and the SLA (service level agreement) come from the same team that builds ERIS.

How will updates reach a system that runs offline?

Upward Technologies plans to send updates to the company through a sandbox. The company installs them on its own servers, and each user's installation then updates from that company server.

What hardware do I need?

Local AI usually needs a GPU server. Its speed depends on that hardware, and existing servers are not always enough. The hardware calculation depends on the AI models you choose.

How many employees can use it?

The published pricing has three company sizes: 10 to 250 staff, 250 to 2,000 staff and 2,000 staff or more. You pay one platform licence for your size plus one price per user.

What about must-have integrations or an outside accountant?

Custom modules, agents and knowledge bases are built for a company as projects and billed separately. Upward Technologies also builds ERP and CRM integrations. Access is set per person, so the assistant answers each person only from the data that person is allowed to open.

Can I switch over gradually?

Yes. According to the ERIS page, a company can replace its current software one module at a time instead of all at once.
